topic: Exact proxy-cumulant depth for latent-confounded LiNGAM effects. For each integer l>=1, observe the joint law of centered (Z,T,Y) generated by the fixed single-proxy graph Z=sum_i a_i L_i+eps_Z, T=gamma Z+sum_i b_i L_i+eps_T, and Y=beta T+sum_i c_i L_i+eps_Y, with mutually independent centered non-Gaussian sources on a generic finite-moment stratum. Let r_beta(l) be the least R for which beta is constant on generic fibers of the complete observed cumulant map through order R. Characterize r_beta(l) exactly: at and above it, give a terminating algebraic beta-recovery map and exceptional discriminant; below it, construct Zariski-open real moment-feasible fibers containing legal independent finite-support unequal-beta twins. Add separated-chart k-statistic/GMM inference and simultaneous polynomial-moment confidence-fiber inversion near collisions. Credit Tramontano--Kivva--Salehkaleybar--Kiyavash--Drton ICML 2025 Theorems 3.1 and 3.4--3.6 for the sufficient k(l) order and their claimed l=1 lower bound, and distinguish the banked bivariate causal-direction frontier. The CEId-from-Moments companion implementation is the same-question consumer: the theorem changes its minimum moment order and adds an instability certificate. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A stacked Z-anchored cumulant factorization A_(R,d)=B E_d was derived; full rank makes its kernel annihilate every finite source and yields beta as a rational contraction ratio. Exact centered-Bernoulli arithmetic gives r_beta(1)=3 and rejects the published quadratic extra root by a nonzero observable identity; exact calculations give 3<=r_beta(2)<=4 and r_beta(3)=4, while rank counting and legal moment charts give asymptotically matching square-root lower and upper depth bounds. Covariance twins, zero-cumulant boundaries, denominator/rank failures, real-versus-complex branches, generic-decomposition collapse, current literature, and neighboring bank entries were checked. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Classify the beta projection of every complete graph-constrained simultaneous ternary-cumulant fiber at intermediate orders, including real moment realizability, to obtain exact finite-l depths and the global lower-fiber theorem. EARLY KILL TEST: Compute the complete saturated beta elimination and exact real moment-feasible fibers for l=2 at R=3 without selecting one polynomial; stop the converse extension if the promised open legal-twin chambers do not exist. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/scm_proxy_cumulant_depth.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the exact least cumulant depth r_beta(l) for generic identification of the treatment effect in the single-proxy latent-confounded LiNGAM with l latent confounders, rather than the presently known sufficient depth k(l).

source_refs.claim: Theorems 3.4–3.5 identify the proxy-model effect from cumulants through k(l), while Theorem 3.6 gives a claimed lower result only for l=1.
source_refs.author: Daniele Tramontano, Yaroslav Kivva, Saber Salehkaleybar, Negar Kiyavash, Mathias Drton

source_refs.claim: Theorem 4 supplies a degree-(l+1) polynomial for a bivariate latent-LiNGAM mixing problem from higher cumulants but does not establish minimality for the graph-constrained ternary proxy effect.
source_refs.author: Daniela Schkoda, Elina Robeva, Mathias Drton

open_problems.why_unsolved: The published upper bound recovers unordered bivariate root lists and then matches latent-source cumulant signatures; this may require orders unnecessary for the complete joint (Z,T,Y) cumulant ideal. Conversely, rank or dimension counts do not prove failure below k(l): necessity requires generic beta-varying fibers whose alternative points obey the graph constraints and are realizable by independent real source distributions with the required finite moments.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact formula for r_beta(l), with a terminating rational or algebraic beta-recovery map and exceptional discriminant at and above the threshold and Zariski-open real moment-feasible unequal-beta fibers below it.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the closest motivation arc and the sufficient-order benchmark that the proposed exact frontier must sharpen.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Latent confounding defeats covariance identification -> non-Gaussian cumulants encode independent-source mixing -> one proxy enables effect recovery at k(l) -> determine the least depth at which recovery is possible.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the higher-order-cumulant rank matrices, annihilating-polynomial construction, and Vandermonde recovery proof to the complete ternary cumulant map rather than three separately solved bivariate maps.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its polynomial roots are the source-loading ratios used by the ICML upper bound, so joint elimination can reveal which cumulant orders are artifacts of pairwise recovery.

method_exemplars.technique: Use elimination ideals and lowest-degree beta relations to distinguish rational identification, finite algebraic identification, and positive-dimensional fibers.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired depth is a fiber-degree transition for a polynomial moment parametrization, matching their algebraic identification framework.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the plug-in k-statistic estimator, polynomial root extraction, and cumulant-signature matching consistency argument after replacing k(l) by the exact minimal depth.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the estimator built for this proxy graph, and its proof shows how a sharper recovery map changes the empirical moment requirement.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether beta is generically identified from the complete order-2-and-3 cumulant map when l=2, including the exact beta projection and real moment feasibility of every saturated fiber component.

source_refs.claim: Theorem 3.5 provides a sufficient cumulant-order bound for multiple confounders, whereas its stated order lower bound concerns only l=1.
source_refs.author: Daniele Tramontano, Yaroslav Kivva, Saber Salehkaleybar, Negar Kiyavash, Mathias Drton

source_refs.claim: The bivariate cumulant construction returns a finite unordered loading-ratio list at a higher order but does not classify the beta projection of the simultaneous ternary R=3 fiber.
source_refs.author: Daniela Schkoda, Elina Robeva, Mathias Drton

open_problems.why_unsolved: For two confounders, the complete mixed ternary cumulants impose compatibility relations absent from the separate bivariate root systems used in the sufficient construction. Saturating by nonzero loadings, variances, and relevant minors can remove spurious components, and imposing real independent-source moment feasibility can remove further beta branches; no located result computes this complete intermediate-order projection.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A saturated elimination and real-feasibility classification for l=2 and R=3 proving a singleton beta projection or exhibiting a Zariski-open real chamber with explicit finite-support unequal-beta twins.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames multiple latent confounders with one proxy as the target problem but supplies only a sufficient depth, making l=2 the first unresolved finite-order stress test.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: One proxy can identify effects despite multiple latent confounders -> the published construction uses increasingly high cumulants -> the first multiconfounder intermediate order remains unclassified -> settle the full l=2, R=3 beta fiber.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply Gröbner elimination with beta retained, saturation by genericity factors, and fiber-degree analysis to the simultaneous moment parametrization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The deliverable is a generic-identifiability decision and recovery relation for one coordinate of a polynomially parametrized causal model.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt moment-variety dimension, secant-defect, and explicit general-fiber calculations to distinguish singleton, finite, and positive-dimensional moment fibers.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Their machinery addresses how truncation order changes generic fibers of polynomial moment maps, which is the core geometry of the l=2 test.

method_exemplars.technique: Use incomplete-U-statistic estimates of cumulant minors and multiplier-bootstrap calibration to test the rank and saturation conditions defining recovered charts.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The algebraic classification becomes statistically usable only if its component-defining rank constraints can be assessed from noisy empirical moments.

open_problems.open_problem: Classify the legal real third-cumulant beta fiber for the l=1 proxy-to-treatment graph and determine whether the quadratic extra beta root in the published lower-bound argument generically corresponds to a second admissible independent-source model.

source_refs.claim: Theorem 3.6 infers nonidentification from orders 2–3 using an elimination relation that is quadratic in beta.
source_refs.author: Daniele Tramontano, Yaroslav Kivva, Saber Salehkaleybar, Negar Kiyavash, Mathias Drton

source_refs.claim: Proposition 3 warns that a higher-degree elimination polynomial need not imply generic statistical nonidentification because parameter-space restrictions may select one admissible root.
source_refs.author: Luis David Garcia-Puente, Sarah Spielvogel, Seth Sullivant

open_problems.why_unsolved: A quadratic beta relation establishes at most two complex algebraic candidates, not two admissible real structural parameter points. Positive source variances and truncated moment sequences realizable by mutually independent non-Gaussian distributions can eliminate an algebraic branch. The lower-bound claim therefore needs either an explicit legal second preimage or a proof that an additional observable identity removes it.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A semialgebraic fiber theorem at R=3 proving either a generic rational beta formula with its nonvanishing denominator or a Zariski-open chamber of finite-support independent-source unequal-beta twins.

writing_exemplar.why: Its Theorem 3.6 is the precise claim under audit and supplies the quadratic-elimination narrative that must be refined from complex roots to admissible statistical fibers.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Fourth-order cumulants suffice in the one-confounder graph -> third-order elimination leaves a quadratic beta relation -> algebraic multiplicity is interpreted as nonidentification -> determine whether both roots are real moment-feasible structural models.

method_exemplars.technique: Compute the saturated elimination ideal and analyze preimages in the original semialgebraic parameter domain instead of inferring statistical multiplicity from polynomial degree.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its Proposition 3 identifies exactly the distinction between algebraic candidate count and the number of admissible parameter fibers.

method_exemplars.technique: Use positive moment matrices and flat extensions to certify and construct finitely atomic representing measures for proposed source-moment sequences.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The missing converse step is real truncated-moment feasibility of the alternative algebraic root.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert singularity-robust nonlinear moment tests instead of selecting one estimated quadratic root, retaining validity when roots merge.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A confidence set for the beta projection remains meaningful whether the population fiber is singleton, two-point, or locally singular.

open_problems.open_problem: Develop inference for the proxy-cumulant beta that is asymptotically normal on separated regular charts yet remains uniformly coverage-valid through root collisions, vanishing denominators, and rank-deficient cumulant strata.

source_refs.claim: Section 4 plugs k-statistics into the identification algorithm and establishes consistency, while the empirical discussion reports high variance and calls for more detailed uncertainty assessment.
source_refs.author: Daniele Tramontano, Yaroslav Kivva, Saber Salehkaleybar, Negar Kiyavash, Mathias Drton

source_refs.claim: Provides nonlinear-moment confidence sets with uniform size control without imposing point identification or nonsingularity.
source_refs.author: Donald W. K. Andrews, Patrik Guggenberger

source_refs.claim: Uses test inversion to construct causal-effect confidence regions that retain uncertainty about the compatible causal structure and discusses linear non-Gaussian models.
source_refs.author: David Strieder, Tobias Freidling, Stefan Haffner, Mathias Drton

open_problems.why_unsolved: The beta map combines polynomial roots, source matching, and rational contractions. These operations are differentiable away from the discriminant, but at coincident roots or near-zero minors the Jacobian loses rank, labels become unstable, and Wald intervals can have arbitrarily poor coverage. General singularity-robust GMM theory does not itself specify the constrained simultaneous cumulant fiber or an implementable inversion of its beta projection.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A two-regime theorem giving a sandwich-covariance root-n limit and valid GMM intervals on separated charts together with a simultaneous polynomial-moment confidence-fiber inversion whose beta projection has uniform asymptotic coverage over collision sequences.

writing_exemplar.why: Its empirical arc juxtaposes consistent point estimation with high variance and unresolved uncertainty for the same graph.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Higher-order cumulants yield a consistent estimator -> empirical cumulants are noisy and high-variance -> root matching becomes unstable near the discriminant -> provide regular-chart limits and collision-robust confidence fibers.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over multiplier bootstrap for incomplete U-statistic cumulant minors and singular-value limit approximations for algebraic rank constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies computable uncertainty machinery for higher-moment rank objects in latent-confounded linear non-Gaussian models.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt singularity-robust nonlinear Anderson–Rubin and conditional quasi-likelihood-ratio inversion to the stacked polynomial cumulant moments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The confidence fiber must remain valid exactly where the cumulant Jacobian is singular and beta is not locally first-order identified.

method_exemplars.technique: Project an inverted goodness-of-fit confidence region over nuisance structural models onto the causal-effect coordinate.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Projection naturally retains multiple structural branches instead of conditioning on one selected polynomial root.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the least effect-identifying cumulant depth under prescribed patterns of vanishing or coincident source cumulants rather than only on the generic distinct-signature stratum.

source_refs.claim: The proof of Theorem 3.4 matches loading-ratio roots across pairs using generic source-cumulant separation; zero or coincident signatures lie in the excluded exceptional set.
source_refs.author: Daniele Tramontano, Yaroslav Kivva, Saber Salehkaleybar, Negar Kiyavash, Mathias Drton

source_refs.claim: For one latent confounder, cross-moment recovery requires a non-Gaussian witness at some order and Gaussian observational laws yield nonidentification, but no multi-source signature-depth frontier is given.
source_refs.author: Yaroslav Kivva, Saber Salehkaleybar, Negar Kiyavash

source_refs.claim: Gives an if-and-only-if full-distribution identifiability characterization for overcomplete ICA, leaving finite cumulant truncation and source-specific zero patterns unresolved.
source_refs.author: Kexin Wang, Anna Seigal

open_problems.why_unsolved: Non-Gaussianity is not a fixed-order signal condition: symmetric sources can have zero odd cumulants, distinct sources can share their initial cumulants, and a source may first separate from another only at a later order. The published matching proof excludes these cases, while full-distribution ICA identifiability does not determine which finite signature suffices for beta or when only nuisance loadings remain ambiguous.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient signature-rank characterization of beta recoverability through order R, with a source-pattern-dependent recovery map and explicit unequal-beta counterexamples whenever the observed cumulant signatures fail the condition.

writing_exemplar.why: Its root-alignment proof makes distinct source cumulants visibly load-bearing and therefore provides a natural motivation for a sharp boundary theorem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Cumulant roots recover source-loading candidates -> distinct source signatures align candidates across observed pairs -> vanishing or colliding signatures break alignment -> characterize exactly when beta remains recoverable.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the linear-space-of-rank-one-symmetric-matrices characterization of overcomplete ICA identifiability to the cumulant tensors whose source coefficients remain nonzero.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides geometric language for deciding which source columns remain distinguishable when some cumulant orders carry no source signal.

method_exemplars.technique: Generalize its cross-moment cancellation identity and Gaussian impossibility construction from one confounder to source-specific cumulant signatures.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It turns the first usable non-Gaussian moment into a direct beta formula, the scalar prototype of a signature-dependent depth theorem.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its cross-moment estimating equations and root-n limit proof to a selected nonvanishing source-signature chart.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a concrete moment-based causal-effect estimator and limit argument for inference after a usable cumulant signature has been located.

literature_map:
Tramontano–Kivva–Salehkaleybar–Kiyavash–Drton (ICML 2025, arXiv:2506.05202) is the direct anchor: Theorems 3.4–3.5 give sufficiency at k(l), while Theorem 3.6 claims the l=1 lower bound.
Schkoda–Robeva–Drton (2024, arXiv:2408.04907) supplies higher-cumulant rank matrices and a bivariate loading polynomial but not the minimal ternary proxy depth.
Garcia-Puente–Spielvogel–Sullivant (UAI 2010, arXiv:1007.3784) creates a sharp tension with the l=1 converse: elimination degree alone need not equal the number of admissible real parameter values.
Kivva–Salehkaleybar–Kiyavash (NeurIPS 2023, arXiv:2306.06263) gives a one-confounder cross-moment formula and Gaussian impossibility result, exposing source-specific non-Gaussian moment order as a boundary.
Salehkaleybar–Ghassami–Kiyavash–Zhang (JMLR 2020, arXiv:1908.03932) and Tramontano et al. (ICML 2024, arXiv:2406.02049) characterize latent-LiNGAM effect ambiguity through overcomplete ICA, but not finite minimal cumulant depth.
Cai–Huang–Chen–Hao–Zhang (ICML 2023, arXiv:2305.19582) and Schkoda–Robeva–Drton replace difficult overcomplete-ICA optimization by higher-cumulant rank conditions under structural restrictions.
Robeva–Seby (SIAM Journal on Applied Algebra and Geometry 2021, doi:10.1137/20M1316470) supplies the multi-trek correspondence between graph structure and higher-order cumulant constraints.
Wang–Seigal (Bernoulli 2026, arXiv:2401.14709) gives full-distribution overcomplete-ICA identifiability, highlighting the missing finite-order and source-signature frontier for a causal functional.
Miao–Geng–Tchetgen Tchetgen (Biometrika 2018, arXiv:1609.08816) identifies effects with two proxies and a rank condition; the single-proxy LiNGAM result instead obtains leverage from non-Gaussian structure.
Cui–Pu–Shi–Miao–Tchetgen Tchetgen (JASA 2024, arXiv:2011.08411) and Kallus–Mao–Uehara (arXiv:2103.14029) show that proxy identification can support efficiency and minimax theory not yet supplied for the cumulant-root model.
Schkoda–Drton (Biometrika 2025, arXiv:2311.04585) develops incomplete-U-statistic and multiplier-bootstrap tests for higher-moment rank constraints, providing a direct inference donor for cumulant charts.
Strieder–Freidling–Haffner–Drton (UAI 2021, arXiv:2106.05694) and Wang–Kolar–Drton (arXiv:2305.14506) use test inversion to retain causal-model uncertainty rather than conditioning on one selected structure.
Andrews–Guggenberger (Quantitative Economics 2019, doi:10.3982/QE1219) supplies identification- and singularity-robust moment inference for cumulant-root collisions and deficient Jacobians.
Curto–Fialkow (Memoirs AMS 1996, doi:10.1090/memo/0568) and Fialkow–Nie (JFA 2012, doi:10.1016/j.jfa.2012.06.004) supply flat-extension tools for separating complex algebraic roots from legal finite-support source moments.
Allman–Matias–Rhodes (Annals of Statistics 2009, arXiv:0809.5032) and Agostini–Améndola–Ranestad (arXiv:1905.05141) exemplify generic-fiber and moment-variety arguments, but no located paper classifies the complete graph-constrained ternary cumulant beta fibers at intermediate orders.
